name: execution_profile
description: One backend the pure-execution tier may hand a closure job to, and what this estate declares about it. A backend here is a compiler target and never an owner: it holds no truth, no identity, no authority, no money, and it cannot perform an effect. The row records what the estate declares -- the kind of reducer it is, whether it is pure, whether it is supposed to be available -- and is deliberately separate from whether the binary is on PATH in this process, because a declared availability is a claim about the estate and presence is a fact about one run. Keeping them apart is what stops a vendored but unbuilt runtime from being mistaken for a running one. The native pure-job.mjs reads execution_profile rows from the CMS and refuses to dispatch when none are readable, which reads as 'the backends are missing' when what is missing is their declaration.
